text:
maria: ran a microprofiling pass on the Llama/Mixtral stack after the weekend deploy — seeing a 12-18% p50 token latency increase on chat templates with long system prompts. attaching a couple of traces and a short summary.

jordan: oh no, regression timeline? did anything change in kernel selection heuristics or batching?

maria: root cause looks multifactorial. quick bullets: kernel selector favored 'matmul_opt_v2' for several layers on Mixtral which is faster for short seqs but ~20% worse once token counts jump due to byte-fallback. batching heuristics: our dynamic batcher extends wait windows when streams hit BOS+system tokens pattern (chat templates), causing slightly larger but less efficient batches. KV cache: hit-rate stays high (~94%) but we see short eviction spikes when token_count_variance > 30% across the batch.

kai: can you paste the profiling snippet? curious about per-op breakdown.

maria: paste:
```
# perf sample for a 4-way batch, Mixtral-8B, seq len 2048 -> 256 tokens gen
99.3% samples: matmul_kernel (matmul_opt_v2) 42ms
  -- fused_attention 18ms
  -- kv_read 6ms
  -- kv_evict 3ms (spikes)
  -- tokenization overhead 12ms (byte-fallback paths)

previous good run (matmul_opt_v1 + fixed small-batches): matmul_kernel 35ms, tokenization 6ms
```

andrew: tokenization doubled in that snippet — likely byte fallback for rare unicode chars in the system prompt? is that reproducible with a sanitized prompt?

maria: yes, sanitized prompt drops tokenization to <8ms and shifts kernel selector to matmul_opt_v1 (our selector uses estimated seq * tokens_per_batch to pick kernel). the byte-fallback path emits lots of small tokens which increases token_count_variance and flips kernel choice.

jordan: two lines of attack: 1) make kernel-selection resilient to tokenization variance (use smoothed distribution not instant estimate) 2) adjust tokenizer fallback: try to avoid per-request fallback by pre-normalizing or memoizing for known templates.

kai: also look at RoPE scaling impact — Mixtral uses a larger RoPE base freq by default for long-context models. If RoPE interpolation changes effective attention weight shape, matmul kernels with different tile sizes hit different memory access patterns. that can flip which kernel is best.

maria: good point — I ran a quick ablation toggling RoPE scaling factor from 1.0 -> 1.06 and saw per-token matmul time change ~5-7ms due to cacheline alignment differences on A100. not huge but enough combined with tokenizer cost to bite.

andrew: for KV cache spikes: are we evicting due to per-shard memory thresholds or an LRU policy thrash because of variable key sizes from byte-fallback tokens?

maria: eviction traces show short-lived LRU churn. the byte-fallback inflates key count when many small tokens are produced, even though total base tokens similar. our KV allocator currently counts entries, not bytes.

jordan: actionable list: 
- change KV allocator to account for bytes in addition to entries (temporary fix)
- smooth kernel-selection metric over last N requests (exponential)
- add a tokenizer normalization pass for common chat templates at the devex layer (to avoid fallback)

devex-bot: FYI: added a small patch to the chat templates repo that normalizes fancy quotes and zero-width chars, link: https://git.internal/redwood/devex/chat-templates/changeset/524

sre-bot: perf-alert suppressed for this regression; scheduled canary with kernel-selector smoothing enabled tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

kai: for model-specific tuning: for Llama 7B we should prefer matmul_opt_v1 for seq>1024 unless token variance < 10%. for Qwen we saw better results with a 64x64 tile kernel when heads*kv_dim > 8192 (empirical). mixtral sits in the middle — we should expose a per-model override map in runtime so we can pin kernels per-model+seq-range.

andrew: agree. also let's add a small sticky cache at tokenizer layer keyed by prompt hash for the last ~1k unique templates. cheap and avoids repeated fallback.

maria: I'll open PRs: runtime kernel selector smoothing + per-model overrides, KV allocator bytes-based accounting, devex normalizer + tokenizer sticky cache. will attach benchmarks.

jordan: prioritize kernel selector and tokenizer sticky cache — these give fastest ROI. KV allocator after.

maria: attaching benchmark summary (short):
- baseline (pre-regress): p50 token latency 18ms, p95 42ms
- regressed: p50 21ms, p95 51ms
- patch1 (tokenizer normalizer + sticky cache): p50 19ms, p95 44ms
- patch2 (kernel-selector smoothing + per-model overrides): p50 17.5ms, p95 40ms
- patch3 (KV bytes accounting): reduces p95 tail spikes for long chats by ~8%

kai: nice. can you include a small repro harness (rng seeds + prompt sample) so infra can run canaries?

maria: will add harness and a short runbook:
1) run repro with 4 parallel streams, 50 iters each, randomize template unicode chars to force fallback
2) compare kernel selection logs (enable runtime debug flag)
3) check KV eviction counters and per-shard bytes

andrew: unblocked for me. call if you want SRE to hold canary window.

jordan: thanks team — let's land the tokenizer/smoothing hotfix and schedule a canary before EOD. :thumbsup:
